sections.label: Questions after Benjamin's death
sections.summary: Benjamin's death raised questions about whether the school did enough and whether Police should have taken him without parental consent or an adult.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the wake of Benjamin's death, there were questions and concerns raised about whether the school had done enough to look after Benjamin's interests and whether the school should have allowed the Police to take Benjamin away without his parents' consent or an accompanying adult.

sections.label: Schools' dual responsibilities for students
sections.summary: When a suspect is a student, schools have dual responsibilities towards the student and to cooperate with Police for public safety and security.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: When a suspect happens to be a student, our schools have dual responsibilities towards the student and also to cooperate with the Police in the interest of public safety and security.

sections.label: Police prerogative, not school
sections.summary: The prerogative lies with the Police, not with the Principal or the school staff.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The prerogative lies with the Police, not with the Principal or the school staff.

sections.label: Request against handcuffs, discreet escort
sections.summary: The school will request the student not be handcuffed and be escorted discreetly, but Police retain final discretion on handcuffs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Fifth, the school will request that the student not be handcuffed and be escorted to the Police vehicle discreetly, with minimal exposure to other students and school staff.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, the Police retain final discretion to use handcuffs, depending on the circumstances of each case.

sections.label: School worked with Police
sections.summary: In Benjamin's case, the school worked with the Police to ensure the relevant steps were taken.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In Benjamin's case, the school worked with the Police to ensure that the relevant steps were taken.

sections.label: No one accompanied Benjamin
sections.summary: The school did not send anyone to accompany Benjamin to the Police station, as Police practice and Protocols do not allow it.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The first concern is that the school did not send anyone to accompany Benjamin to the Police station.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, it is not the practice of the Police to allow teachers or school staff to be with the student in the Police car.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Furthermore, current Police Protocols do not allow other persons to be present when the student is undergoing questioning at the Police station.

sections.label: Benjamin and school camp decision
sections.summary: The camp was on 27 January, the day after Benjamin was asked to assist the Police, and the counsellor asked his mother if he should stay with family.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This leads me to the second concern relating to the decision for Benjamin not to attend the school camp.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: This camp was to be held on 27 January, the very next day after Benjamin was asked to assist the Police.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As such, when the school counsellor called Benjamin's mother on the afternoon of 26 January to check on Benjamin's well-being, the counsellor also raised with Benjamin's mother if it would be better for Benjamin to remain with his family during this difficult period.

sections.label: Adapting school processes after review
sections.summary: School processes will be adapted to align with review recommendations, including possibly having a school staff as an Appropriate Adult at the Police station.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Where needed, we will adapt and refine our school processes to align them with the recommendations arising from this review, including, if the review so concludes, the presence of a school staff as an Appropriate Adult at the Police station.

sections.label: Youths picked up for offences
sections.summary: The Minister indicated that more than 1,300 youths are picked up for various offences every year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Minister also indicated that, every year, more than 1,300 youths are picked up for various offences.

sections.label: Youths picked up for rioting
sections.summary: Over 500 were picked up for rioting involving serious gang activities in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If my memory serves me right, about maybe over 500 were picked up for rioting in the last five years, rioting involving serious gang activities.

sections.label: Guidance Programmes for youths
sections.summary: About 600 youths a year go to six-month Guidance Programmes instead of being charged, and 89% go on to lead crime-free lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At the same time, our own research and approach show that, at a young age, the criminality or criminal conduct can, with the right approach, be limited in time or limited by age.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why we send a very large number − again, if my memory serves me right − about 600 per year to Guidance Programmes where, in return for not proceeding with a charge, they have to undergo a six-month Guidance Programme, about 20-over sessions where they are taken through the need to understand the nature of the act involved, including the criminality, the impact on the community, how to manage themselves better in their social interactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This is a programme that, in a way, of course, involves the AGC and MSF.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That means 89% go on to lead crime-free lives.

sections.label: Boy brought to Principal's office
sections.summary: The boy was brought to the Principal's office, interviewed with the educators present, then taken back to the Police station in an unmarked car.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The boy was brought to the Principal's office; he was interviewed in the presence of the educators and then, he was brought back to the Police station in an unmarked car.

sections.label: Review timing and Coroner's Inquiry
sections.summary: The review will start but decisions will wait until after the Coroner's Inquiry, and stakeholders may be consulted.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first point as to when the review would be completed, I have told my officials that we should start the work but we should hold back on any decisions until after the Coroner's Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Let the Coroner's Inquiry go through, let there be a finding, we will take reference from that.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The second thing that we need to do and that is why I do not want to rush into it, is also maybe consult the stakeholders.

sections.label: Guidance Programme results
sections.summary: The Guidance Programme has an 89% success rate and 11% recidivism.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why we place a lot of emphasis on the Guidance Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are very pleased with the results of the Guidance Programme at 89% success rate; but 11% recidivism.

sections.label: Suggestions and process review
sections.summary: All suggestions will be looked at to improve the process, but the processes cannot be said to have led to this result.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we will look at all suggestions to see how our process can be made better.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I do want to emphasise this, on the facts today, I cannot say that it was the processes that led to this tragic result.

sections.label: Family prefers private Coroner's Inquiry
sections.summary: On 24 February, he told officers the family would prefer to keep the Coroner's Inquiry private.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 24 February last week, he had told us in the presence of a number of officers that the family would prefer to keep the Coroner's Inquiry private.

sections.label: Family's requests remain
sections.summary: He said the family's earlier requests remained: no media harassment, privacy respected, and a private Coroner's Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He told us yesterday that the family's earlier set of requests remained.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He continued with the request that the media not harass him, that the family's privacy be respected and that the Coroner's Inquiry be held in private.

sections.label: Extending current scheme scope
sections.summary: Despite the scheme possibly being imperfect, the Minister is asked to consider extending its scope.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the fact that it could be an imperfect scheme, I would like to ask the Minister to consider extending the scope of this current scheme.

sections.label: Review of Appropriate Adult presence
sections.summary: The review will cover whether an Appropriate Adult should be present when young persons are interviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Yes, that is something that we would look at.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first point, I have already said that both in my Statement and in answer to Dr Tan's question, that the review would cover this particular aspect as whether an Appropriate Adult should be present when young persons are interviewed.

sections.label: Contempt law applies online
sections.summary: The law of contempt on reporting before a pending hearing or inquiry is the same online and offline.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The law is the same on reporting before a pending hearing or inquiry; whether it is a physical world or online world, the law of contempt is the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Just because you are online does not mean that you get a free pass and you can say what you like.

sections.label: Allegations of disputed fact
sections.summary: Allegations of fact cannot be made when those facts could be disputed or decided in an inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What you cannot do is to make allegations of fact when those facts could be the subject matter of dispute or have to be found in an inquiry or would necessarily be part of what an inquiry would have to decide.

sections.label: MOE staff accompanying students
sections.summary: A Member asks if MOE would assign staff to accompany a student brought to a Police station.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: We will now proceed to clarifications on the Statement made by the Minister for Education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We understand that the Police is doing a review, but while Police is doing the review, would MOE consider assigning an MOE staff to accompany a student if he is brought back to the Police station from school, even though MOE staff may not be able to be in the same Police car or during the interview at the Police station.

sections.label: MOE considering staff accompaniment
sections.summary: If the Appropriate Adult recommendation is made, MOE will consider getting its staff to be with the student.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: If the Appropriate Adult accompanying is part of any recommendation, MOE will certainly consider getting our staff to be with the student.

sections.label: Principals lack discretion
sections.summary: Under the current process, Principals have no such discretion under the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In the current process, the Principals under the law have no such discretion.

sections.label: Statistics on school cases
sections.summary: Over the last three years, across all schools, the number is close to 1,500 per year, about 4,500 over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For the statistics: over the last three years or so, across all the different schools, we have close to 1,500 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: So, it is about 4,500 over three years.

sections.label: Police interviewing students in school
sections.summary: The interview was during school hours, and under current Singapore laws no parental consent is needed for Police to interview a student or any person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: To the first question, Mdm Speaker, the answer is yes, it was during school hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With the current laws of Singapore, there is no need for consent from the parents when Police want to interview a student or any person in particular.

sections.label: Counsellor consulting mother about Benjamin
sections.summary: For such an incident, processes are in place for the counsellor to consult the mother about how Benjamin is doing, which is very reasonable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For such an incident where the processes are in place for the counsellor to consult with the mother to see how Benjamin is doing, it is very reasonable.

sections.label: Decision on Benjamin attending camp
sections.summary: The decision for Benjamin to go to camp or not was discussed and mutually agreed upon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Even then, the decision for Benjamin to go to camp or not, was one that was discussed and mutually agreed upon.

sections.label: Cases handled case-by-case
sections.summary: Currently, the cases are handled on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Currently, the cases are handled on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Counselling referrals and tailored regime
sections.summary: Referrals are made to FSCs for further counselling beyond school, and the Member's suggestion on a regime tailored to such students will be taken up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: If there is a need for further counselling besides the school and beyond the school, referrals are made to the FSCs to extend this help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But, certainly, I will take up the Member's suggestion on whether a regime could be set up to better tailor to the needs of such students.
